name: Albuquerque Apparel Center
old_description: Albuquerque Apparel Center is an infrastructure tailored to meet the needs of designers, suppliers, production houses, merchants, and visitors with a wide range of useful customized products and services.  We are New Mexico’s premier venue of clothing and accessory design as well as supplies, services and events.
about:
Albuquerque Apparel Center operates in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a statewide hub for the apparel and accessory industry. The organization does not disclose a founding year, ownership structure, or founder names in its public materials. It was established to connect designers, suppliers, production houses, and merchants across New Mexico, providing a physical and online infrastructure for the sector.

The center delivers a range of services rather than manufactured goods. It runs a networking hub that promotes New Mexico apparel through events, fashion shows, and multi-media advertising. A physical location allows designers to sell directly to retail customers while accessing wholesale buyers. The online platform NMFashionInfo.com serves as a directory for stores, supplies, services, and events statewide. The center also offers custom design and pattern services, operates the AAC School of Fashion Design with classes in flat pattern drafting, draping, and sewing, and provides mentorship programs. Community initiatives include fashion design classes for battered women's groups and rehabilitation facilities.

Its audience spans the fashion and apparel industry: independent designers, start-up brands, production houses, suppliers, merchants, and students. The center also works with social-service organizations to deliver vocational training. Customers include New Mexico-based apparel companies and individuals seeking education, networking, or promotional support.

The organization states its mission is to foster growth of New Mexico's apparel industry by connecting local companies, guiding start-ups, and providing education. It positions itself as a support system for talent that otherwise lacks infrastructure, aiming to make New Mexico a recognized fashion center leveraging the state's lower cost of living and distinctive Southwest, Native American, and Western styles.
